title: अष्ट्रेलियामा बसोवास गर्ने गैर आवासीय नेपाली संघको  भूमिका {The role of non-resident Nepalese associations in Australia}
authors: बस्याल Basyal, ध्रुब प्रसाद Dhruba Prasad
nepali: मानब विकासको इतिहास भन्नु नै बसाइ सराइको इतिहास हो । बसाइ सराइ भनेको आफ्नो थातथलो छोडेर नया स्थानमा जानु हो । बसाइ सराइका कारण आर्थिक, सामाजिक र राजनैतिक कारणहरु हुन्छन । सन् १९९० पछि नवउदारबाद र भुमण्डलीकरणले गर्दा बसाइ सराइको विगतको भन्दा फरक चरित्र र आयामहरु देखा परेका छन । विगतमा मूलथलो छोडेपछि फर्केर आउने वा सम्र्पकमा रहने चलन ज्यादै कम थियो । हालको वैदेशिक बसाई सराइले कसरी आफ्नो मूलथलो र कर्मथलो जोड्छ भन्ने वारेमा समाजशास्त्रीय बुझाइ कम छ । नेपालको इतिहास हेर्ने हो भने आर्थिक अथवा धार्मिक कार्यको लागि आÇनो देश छोडेर विदेश जाने क्रम ज्यादै पुरानो रहेको पाइन्छ । आजको जस्तो अमेरिका, अष्ट्रेलिया, बेलायत, जापान, कोरिया जाने चलन प्रायः थिएन । बसाइ सराइ पहाडवाट तराइतिर र भारत तथा म्यानमारसम्म सिमित थियो । हाल करिब ८० लाख नेपाली विदेशमा रहेको अनुमान छ । गैर आवासिय नेपाली सम्वन्धमा नेपाली सामाजिकशास्त्री र समाजशास्त्रीहरुले यस क्षेत्रमा खासै अनुसन्धान गरेको पाइदैन । गैर आवासिय नेपालीहरुले तिनीहरुको जन्मस्थानसंग कसरी निरन्तर संम्पर्कमा रहिरहन्छन भन्ने वारेको बुझाइ ज्यादै कम पाइन्छ । हालैका दिनमा अष्ट्रेलिया जाने र उतै बसोवास गर्ने नेपालीहरुको संख्या दिनानुदिन बढीरहेको छ । गैर आवासिय नेपाली संघका वारेमा पत्रपत्रिका तथा राजनितिक भाषणमा धेरै चलन चल्तीमा आएको भएता पनि यो संघको विधानमा के के कुरा समावेस छन, नेपाल सरकारको कानुनमा गैर आवासिय नेपाली वारेमा के ब्यवस्था छ भन्ने वारे जानकारी कम रहेको छ । यहि विषय वस्तुलाई ध्यानमा राखि प्रस्तुत लेखले अष्ट्रेलियामा बसोवास गर्ने नेपालीहरु कसरी एक आपसमा आबध्द भई अष्ट्रेलियन नेपालीको पहिचान बनाएका छन् भन्ने वारे प्रकाश पार्नु यस लेखको उद्येश्य रहेको छ । यस अध्ययनको लागि प्राथमिक तथा द्वितियक तथ्यांक संकलन गरिएको छ । लेखक स्वयं अध्ययनका क्रममा अष्ट्रेलियामा बस्दाको अनुभव, अवलोकन तथा अष्ट्रेलियामा बसोवास गर्नेहरुसंगको अन्र्तवार्तामा आधारित छ ।
american_english: The history of human development is essentially the history of migration. Migration means leaving one's ancestral home and going to a new place. The reasons for migration are economic, social, and political factors. Since 1990, due to neoliberalism and globalization, different characteristics and dimensions of migration from those in the past have emerged. In the past, the practice of returning or staying in touch after leaving one's place of origin was very rare. There is little sociological understanding regarding how present-day foreign migration links one's homeland and one's workplace. Looking at the history of Nepal, the practice of leaving one's country and going abroad for economic or religious pursuits is found to be very old. The trend of going to America, Australia, Britain, Japan, and Korea as seen today was practically non-existent. Migration was limited from the hills toward the Tarai, and up to India and Myanmar. Currently, it is estimated that around 8 million Nepalis are abroad. Regarding Non-Resident Nepalis, it is found that Nepali social scientists and sociologists have hardly conducted research in this field. There is very little understanding of how Non-Resident Nepalis remain in continuous contact with their birthplace. In recent days, the number of Nepalis going to Australia and settling there has been increasing day by day. Even though the Non-Resident Nepali Association has become widely cited in newspapers and political speeches, information remains limited about what is contained in this association's constitution and what provisions exist regarding Non-Resident Nepalis in the laws of the Government of Nepal. Bearing this subject matter in mind, the objective of this article is to shed light on how Nepalis residing in Australia have bonded together and formed an Australian-Nepali identity. Primary and secondary data have been collected for this study. It is based on the author's own experience and observations while living in Australia during the course of the study, as well as interviews with people residing in Australia.

informal_english: The history of human progress is basically just the history of migration. Migration simply means leaving your ancestral home and heading off to a new place. The reasons for migration come down to economic, social, and political factors. Since 1990, with neoliberalism and globalisation taking off, different characteristics and dimensions of migration from those in the past have emerged. In the past, the practice of returning or staying in touch after leaving one's place of origin was very rare indeed. There is little sociological understanding regarding how present-day foreign migration links one's homeland and one's workplace. Looking at the history of Nepal, the practice of leaving one's country and heading abroad for economic or religious pursuits goes back donkey's years. The trend of going to America, Australia, Britain, Japan, and Korea as seen today was practically non-existent. Migration was limited from the hills towards the Tarai, and up to India and Myanmar. Currently, around 8 million Nepalis are estimated to be abroad. Regarding Non-Resident Nepalis, it is found that Nepali social scientists and sociologists have hardly done any proper research in this field. There is precious little understanding of how Non-Resident Nepalis remain in continuous contact with their birthplace. In recent days, the number of Nepalis heading to Australia and settling down there has been climbing day by day. Even though the Non-Resident Nepali Association has become widely cited in newspapers and political speeches, information remains limited about what is contained in this association's constitution and what provisions exist regarding Non-Resident Nepalis in the laws of the Government of Nepal. Bearing this subject matter in mind, the whole point of this article is to shed light on how Nepalis residing in Australia have bonded together and formed an Australian-Nepali identity. Both primary and secondary data have been collected for this study. It is based on the author's own experience and observations whilst living in Australia during the course of the study, plus interviews with people residing in Australia.
